reading.body:
Flexential Louisville - East publishes 1.46 MW of IT capacity across 33,588 square feet of technical space. At 10 kW per rack, a common colocation density, that load supports roughly 146 racks; at 40 kW per rack, a density more typical of AI training workloads, it supports roughly 37 racks. Those figures are assumptions about rack density, not operator claims. The footprint is modest, and the published capacity does not suggest a facility built around large-scale AI training clusters.

The certification stack qualifies this campus to host a specific set of regulated workloads. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 address financial and operational controls. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment card data. ITAR qualifies it for export-controlled defense and aerospace data. NIST 800-53 and HITRUST together cover federal security frameworks and healthcare information. SSAE 18 is the auditing standard underlying the SOC reports rather than a separate capability.

Kentucky has five data center facilities mapped in this site's coverage, three of which publish a megawatt figure, totaling 9.55 MW across those three. Flexential Louisville - East contributes 1.46 MW of that total, placing it third by published IT capacity in the state. That rank and share reflect only what operators have published to this site, not the full picture of Kentucky's data center market. At 1.46 MW, this campus is not a meaningful factor in AI infrastructure at scale, but its compliance certifications position it for regulated enterprise workloads that AI deployments in healthcare, defense, or financial services may require as adjacent infrastructure.
